name: pom
description: PEG parser combinators using operator overloading for a grammar-like syntax

license.comment: Cargo.toml declares license = "MIT"; GitHub reports spdx MIT. Single license.

approach.comment: Self-described as 'PEG parser combinators using operator overloading without macros'; parsers are Rust values composed with +, -, *, >>, |, -p, !p. Tagged both because PEG semantics (ordered choice, lookahead) are documented explicitly.

implementation.comment: Only dependency is bstr (pure Rust). No C/C++ in the tree.

documentation.comment: docs.rs is the API reference (80% doc coverage on 3.4.0); a long-form tutorial article lives in doc/article.md of the repository.

latest-stable-version.comment: Checked 2026-09-19; 3.4.0 published 2024-03-06. master Cargo.toml already reads 3.4.1 but that version is unpublished. All research reflects pom 3.4.x.

grammar-class.comment: Documents PEG semantics explicitly (ordered choice via |, positive/negative lookahead via -p and !p), so tagged 'peg' rather than 'arbitrary' per Assessment Guidelines. The monadic >> operator additionally allows context-sensitive parsing beyond strict PEG.

grammar-definition.comment: Grammar is plain Rust expressions with overloaded operators; explicitly 'without macros'.

left-recursion.comment: No Pratt/precedence helper; recursion goes through call() and a left-recursive rule loops forever. Tutorial notes a Packrat/memoization attempt was abandoned; cache() memoizes but does not handle left recursion.

ambiguity-handling.comment: p | q returns the first alternative that succeeds (PEG first-match).

backtracking.comment: Alternatives backtrack freely by default; .expect(name) marks a parser as committed and produces Error::Expect, which aborts the enclosing ordered choice (a cut).

lexer-integration.comment: Scannerless over &[u8] / &str (utf8 module). Parser<'a, I, O> is generic over the symbol type I, so an external lexer's token slice (&[Token]) can be parsed directly; not an Iterator adapter, requires a slice.

precedence-pratt-support.comment: No operator-precedence facility; expression grammars must encode precedence levels as separate rules.

unicode-aware.comment: The utf8 module (default feature) provides char-level sym/any/one_of/is_a etc. over UTF-8 bytes via bstr::decode_utf8, and take()/skip() count chars and reject ranges that split a character. The base parser module is byte-oriented.

input-types.comment: parse(&'a [I]) for any symbol type (bytes, tokens); utf8::Parser adds parse_str(&'a str). No custom input trait, no rope support.

streaming-partial-input.comment: Error::Incomplete exists and is returned when input ends mid-match, but there is no resumable/partial-input API; the whole slice must be present.

zero-copy.comment: .collect() yields &input[start..end] (&'a [I] / &'a str) borrowed from the input.

span-tracking.comment: Single byte offsets only: .pos() returns the position after a match and every error variant carries position: usize. No ranges, no line/column.

output-model.comment: Each Parser<I, O> produces an arbitrary Rust O; README's JSON example builds a JsonValue enum directly.

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: No implicit skipping; README's JSON example defines a space() parser and sequences it explicitly (e.g. space() * value - space()).

stateful-parsing.comment: No user-state parameter; parsers are Box<dyn Fn(&[I], usize) -> Result<(O, usize)>>. Only closure captures could carry state.

error-recovery.comment: Parsing stops at the first failure and returns a single Error; no skip/sync or recovery API.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: Result<O> = Result<O, pom::Error>; one error per run (nested inner errors are a chain for a single failure, not multiple errors).

expected-token-reporting.comment: Errors are message strings (e.g. 'expect: X, found: Y' from sym/seq) plus a position; ordered choice reports only the last alternative's error, no aggregated expected set.

custom-error-types.comment: Error type is the fixed pom::Error enum (Incomplete/Mismatch/Conversion/Expect/Custom); .convert() folds user errors into a Conversion message string.

error-span-fidelity.comment: Every error variant except Incomplete carries a single position: usize byte offset plus a message; no ranges or secondary spans (Assessment Guideline: 3 = single offset).

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: No optional dependencies or documented bridges to ariadne/miette/codespan-reporting/annotate-snippets.

contextual-error-messages.comment: .name(label) wraps failures in Error::Custom with the label and inner error; .expect(label) produces Error::Expect. The 'trace' feature prints named-parser activity to stderr.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Produces user-typed values; whitespace is consumed by explicit parsers.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: No editor or language server among the 28 direct dependents listed on lib.rs (checked 2026-09-19).

runtime-speed-tier.comment: No qualifying benchmark. The README table shows pom json_byte ~621 µs/iter vs a pest figure of ~13 µs/iter, but the pest bench is not in the repo's benches/ (only json.rs and json_char.rs) so it is not reproducible; epage/parse-benchmarks-rs dropped pom ('lack of notoriety'). The maintainer's own numbers suggest a 'slow' tier but this is unverified.

compile-time-impact.comment: No published measurement found. Design (boxed dyn Fn closures, ~1.5K LOC, one dependency) implies a light footprint, but per Assessment Guidelines a guess is not recorded.

allocation-strategy.comment: Every combinator boxes a closure at construction; repeat()/list() build Vecs; errors allocate message Strings; cache() uses a RefCell<HashMap>. .collect() borrows, but a typical parse allocates per rule.

no-std-support.comment: No #![no_std]; result.rs imports std::error and the Result alias is ::std::result::Result. No alloc-only feature.

msrv.comment: No rust-version in Cargo.toml and none stated in README; edition = 2021 implies at least Rust 1.56 but no MSRV policy is published.

unsafe-usage.comment: No forbid(unsafe_code). parser.rs has no unsafe; utf8.rs uses str::from_utf8_unchecked on slices already validated via bstr::decode_utf8.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: Explicitly 'without macros'; no proc-macro crates in the dependency list.

wasm-compatible.comment: Inferred, not CI-verified: pure Rust, std-only (no I/O, threads or platform APIs), single pure-Rust dependency bstr; nothing target-specific in the crate.

async-friendly.comment: Parser wraps Box<dyn Fn(...) + 'a> with no Send/Sync bound, so parsers are not Send; input must be a complete in-memory slice.

crates-io-downloads.comment: All-time downloads checked 2026-09-19 (~4.0M recent). Much of the volume comes from PDF-tooling dependents (adobe-cmap-parser, type1-encoding-parser pin pom 1.x).

maintenance-status.comment: Last release 2024-03-06; last commits 2025-01-24 (clippy/doc fixes merged by the owner) and 2024-12-09 (trace output fix). No release or substantive commit in the last 6 months; contributor PRs are still merged. Not archived, no successor named.

documentation-quality.comment: docs.rs reference at 80% item coverage with short one-line method docs, a README operator table plus full JSON example, and one long-form tutorial article. No cookbook or migration guides.

tutorial-book.comment: doc/article.md 'PEG Parser Combinators Implemented in Rust' walks through design, operators and a JSON parser; README also links Bodil Stokke's 'Learning Parser Combinators With Rust'.

notable-users.value: svgbob (ASCII-to-SVG diagram converter), adobe-cmap-parser and type1-encoding-parser (font/CMap parsers used by pdf-extract), chumsky (dev-dependency for its benchmark suite)
notable-users.comment: Verified from Cargo.toml / crates.io. pom was originally written for the author's lopdf, which no longer depends on it.

bus-factor.comment: Single owner/releaser (J-F-Liu). lib.rs lists 17 contributors; nigeleke authored most 2024 changes but releases and merges go through the owner.
